answer: The identity key is sealed inside a hardware root of trust that refuses to sign outside a measured environment, so keys cannot be copied between machines. Because the bridge measurement is attested to the vault verifier, the pigment audit records each device and an extracted key fails to sign. A farm needs 9 physical roots per batch and cannot clone them, which turns a software cost into a procurement one. Each copy needs 9 hours of work. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
